Deputy Director, Product Platforms
GLOBALFOUNDRIES
Richardson
About GlobalFoundries:
GlobalFoundries is a leading full-service semiconductor foundry providing a unique combination of design, development, and fabrication services to some of the world’s most inspired technology companies. With a global manufacturing footprint spanning three continents, GlobalFoundries makes possible the technologies and systems that transform industries and give customers the power to shape their markets. For more information, visit www.gf.com.
Summary of Role:
The Deputy Director, Product Platforms will be the entrepreneurial product leader for a differentiated compute-platform portfolio. The role combines product vision, market insight, technical depth, customer leadership, ecosystem development, and commercial accountability. The successful candidate will turn reusable processor, memory, interconnect, security, safety, AI acceleration, I/O, software, and development-tool assets into compelling customizable platform families and derivative products that customers can adopt and scale.
This is not a product-planning-only role. The leader will engage deeply across hardware and software, work directly with customers and partners, drive disciplined product execution, and remain accountable for successful launches, design wins, adoption, and sustained revenue growth.
Essential responsibilities:
Define and own the multi-year platform vision, product strategy, roadmap, business plan, and investment priorities for the 12nm compute portfolio.
Maintain an architecture and IP-reuse strategy that is anchored in 12nm but can extend to an adjacent process node when supported by market demand, customer requirements, performance / power / cost needs, supply strategy, or portfolio economics.
Translate market trends and customer use cases into platform requirements spanning CPU architecture, memory hierarchy, coherent interconnect / NoC, accelerators, high-speed I/O, security, functional safety, package, power, software, tools, and reference systems.
Create a coherent platform family and derivative strategy rather than isolated one-off products; define where configuration, customer IP integration, chiplets, companion devices, or custom derivatives create differentiated value.
Own product requirements, target specifications, competitive positioning, pricing strategy, business cases, lifecycle plans, and clear go / no-go recommendations.
Lead cross-functional platform execution with architecture, silicon design, verification, physical design, DFT, package, test, validation, software, applications, operations, quality, finance, sales, and marketing.
Drive the full launch process from concept and business approval through platform definition, development, pre-silicon enablement, sampling, production release, market launch, customer ramp, and post-launch optimization.
Build the whole-product plan, including virtual platforms, FPGA prototypes, evaluation systems, SDKs, Linux / RTOS enablement, drivers, toolchains, reference designs, documentation, training, and field collateral.
Develop and manage an ecosystem of processor / IP providers, EDA partners, OS and middleware vendors, toolchain and debug partners, design services firms, board partners, distributors, and application-domain partners.
Establish executive-level relationships with strategic customers and partners; lead discovery, roadmap alignment, product definition, commercial framing, design-win strategy, and escalation resolution.
Partner with sales and field teams to build the opportunity pipeline, segment target accounts, improve customer identification and win rate, and convert early engagements into design wins and production revenue.
Own platform KPIs, including roadmap execution, launch readiness, design wins, qualified pipeline, ecosystem readiness, customer adoption, gross margin, forecast accuracy, revenue growth, and return on investment.
Continuously assess competitive offerings, technology shifts, market inflections, and build / buy / partner choices; adjust the roadmap with speed and discipline.
Communicate a clear, credible platform narrative to executives, customers, partners, field teams, and engineering organizations, balancing vision with evidence and execution realism.
Commercial judgment: ability to balance NRE and customer specific developments with a platform reuse approach, derivative economics, margin, schedule, customer specificity, and long-term portfolio leverage.
Other Responsibilities:
Perform all activities in a safe and responsible manner and support all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security requirements and programs.
Required Qualifications:
Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a closely related technical field; advanced technical or business degree is a plus.
8+ years of semiconductor, embedded-computing, processor, SoC, platform, or closely related product experience, including 5+ years in product management, platform leadership, product marketing, applications, systems, or a comparable customer-facing technical leadership role.
Strong background in 32-bit or 64-bit compute products, with 64-bit MPU, application-processor, edge-compute, infrastructure, or Linux-class product experience strongly preferred.
Demonstrated understanding of SoC hardware and software, including prior hands-on or leadership involvement in both domains. Experience may include silicon architecture, systems, applications, firmware, BSP / SDK, operating systems, drivers, validation, or product engineering.
Proven record of successful semiconductor or embedded-platform launches, from market definition and requirements through customer adoption and production ramp.
Demonstrated product revenue growth, design-win creation, portfolio expansion, or turnaround results supported by concrete business metrics.
Experience creating or scaling a software, tools, IP, and partner ecosystem around a compute product or platform.
Strong customer and partner relationships, with the credibility to engage engineering leaders, product executives, architects, procurement, and business decision makers.
Ability to build rigorous market models, product P&Ls, pricing and margin frameworks, investment cases, forecast ranges, and measurable launch plans.
Excellent leadership and influence skills across matrixed organizations; able to align strong technical and commercial stakeholders without relying solely on direct authority.
Clear executive communication, strong judgment under uncertainty, high ownership, and willingness to move between strategy, detail, and customer execution.
Preferred Qualification:
Experience with RISC-V, Arm, MIPS, or comparable processor architectures; multicore SoCs; MMUs and virtualization; coherent fabrics; cache / DDR subsystems; PCIe, Ethernet, SerDes, or other high-speed interfaces.
Experience with Linux-class products and software enablement, including boot flow, firmware, drivers, SDKs, virtual platforms, FPGA prototyping, evaluation boards, and developer tooling.
Exposure to AI / ML acceleration, vector processing, edge inference, networking offload, functional safety, cybersecurity, HSM / root of trust, or long-lifecycle industrial and automotive products.
Experience managing process-node, foundry, package, test, yield, cost, supply, and lifecycle tradeoffs for semiconductor products.
Experience with configurable platforms, product derivatives, custom silicon, customer IP integration, or platform reuse across multiple end markets.
Established network across customers and ecosystem partners in edge compute, industrial, robotics, machine vision, infrastructure or automotive.
Experience leading geographically distributed teams and operating across engineering, field, partner, and executive communities.
Leadership Profile
Visionary and market-back
Connects technology inflections and customer pain points to a differentiated, investable platform roadmap.
Self-motivated owner
Creates momentum, closes gaps, and drives decisions without waiting for a fully defined playbook.
Technical product leader
Can challenge architects and software leaders while translating tradeoffs into customer and business outcomes.
Commercially accountable
Treats launch, adoption, margin, and revenue as core product responsibilities, not downstream sales tasks.
Ecosystem builder
Understands that processors win through software, tools, partners, reference systems, and developer confidence.
Customer credible
Builds trust through preparation, transparency, technical command, and reliable follow-through.
Platform thinker
Optimizes for reuse and scalable derivatives while recognizing when a strategic customer-specific investment is justified.
Decisive and adaptable
Makes evidence-based decisions with incomplete information, explicitly manages risk, and adjusts quickly as facts change.
Success Measures
Clear, approved platform strategy and roadmap with explicit market, customer, product, software, ecosystem, financial, and process-node choices.
Launch milestones achieved with measurable readiness across silicon, software, tools, boards, documentation, field enablement, supply, and quality.
Priority customer opportunities converted into architecture engagements, design wins, and credible production-revenue paths.
Platform and derivative portfolio demonstrates disciplined reuse of IP, software, validation, infrastructure, and commercial investments.
Ecosystem gaps identified early and closed through internal development, licensing, co-development, or strategic partnerships.
Revenue, margin, design-win pipeline, product adoption, and portfolio return improve against agreed business targets.
Field, customer, partner, and engineering teams operate from one product narrative, one prioritized roadmap, and transparent decision gates.
Preferred Target Talent Pools
Product or platform leaders from embedded processor, MPU, BMC, industrial compute, vision SoC, networking, data-center infrastructure, or edge-AI semiconductor companies.
Experience with products serving multiple markets rather than only a single customer or single vertical.
Experience with customer-funded or anchor-funded platform development models, derivative roadmaps, and ecosystem/software readiness.
Customer-facing credibility with engineering, architecture, platform, and advanced technology teams.
The strongest candidate will combine engineering credibility, whole-product hardware/software judgment, customer and ecosystem leadership, successful launch evidence, and quantified revenue ownership. 64-bit product experience is preferred, but an exceptional 32-bit platform leader with credible SW/Market Focos/ Linux / MPU adjacency should remain in scope.
Expected Salary Range
$171,000.00 - $296,000.00
The exact Salary will be determined based on qualifications, experience and location.

Director, Contract Manufacturing Operations
Aether
United States
$140,000.00/yr - $200,000.00/yr
About Aether
Aether engineers enzymes and uses them to make materials that are difficult or impossible to produce any other way. The long-term goal is to manufacture more or less anything, quickly and cheaply, anywhere, by drawing on a few billion years of evolution rather than inventing the chemistry from scratch. Today that work pays for itself through advanced print materials. These are shipping into defense and unmanned systems, with revenue and strong customer feedback. Aether is a Series A company that has raised a little over $60M, with a small team based in the San Francisco Bay Area.
The role
Aether manufactures its materials through a network of contract manufacturing organizations (CMOs), covering everything from chemical synthesis through compounding and finished material production. This role owns that network day to day. The VP of Manufacturing selects and qualifies CMO partners. From there, you make sure each partner delivers what it committed to: on time, on spec, and at the agreed cost.
You’ll be Aether’s representative on site at each partner. You’ll know the production plan at every CMO, keep partners accountable to their contracts, and act quickly when things go off track. This role works at the level of plant and site leadership. It’s the counterpart to our process engineers, who work with CMO engineering teams on the technical details. You’ll also keep manufacturing execution in line with commercial demand, so that what Aether sells is what the network can actually produce.
This is one of the first hires in a new manufacturing organization. You’ll be setting how Aether manages its CMO partners for years to come.
What you’ll do
Own day-to-day performance of Aether’s CMO network across multiple sites and production stages.
Ensure each partner has credible production plans that meet Aether’s schedule, specifications, and cost targets.
Hold partners accountable to supply agreements, and escalate and resolve issues directly with site and plant leadership.
Be on site for production campaigns and new CMO onboarding, and support the VP of Manufacturing in standing up new partners.
Coordinate schedules and handoffs between partners where different stages of production happen at different sites.
Translate commercial demand into production plans the CMO network can execute, in partnership with the commercial and supply chain teams.
Track partner performance on delivery, cost, and output, and report it to manufacturing leadership.
Work with quality and process engineering so that CMO execution reflects Aether’s specifications and process requirements.
What you bring
10+ years in manufacturing operations, with significant time managing contract manufacturers or outsourced production.
Experience in chemicals, polymers, specialty materials, or similar process industries.
A track record of holding external partners to commitments. You’re comfortable escalating to plant leadership and can do it without damaging the relationship.
Working fluency in supply agreements, production scheduling, and manufacturing cost drivers.
Strong organizational and program management skills across multiple sites at once.
Willingness to travel 30 to 50% of the time.
Nice to have
Experience working at a CMO or tolling facility, so you know the other side of the table.
Experience at an early-stage or fast-growing company.
Familiarity with ISO 9001 quality systems.
Note
The pay range for this role is $140,000 to $200,000 per year plus equity, with final compensation based on skills and experience.
Aether is committed to building an inclusive and diverse workplace. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and do not discriminate on the basis of age, disability, gender identity or expression, marital or civil-partner status, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation. All employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs.
We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates throughout the recruitment process. If you require any adjustments to participate fully in interviews or assessments, please let us know and we will work with you to support your needs.

Shield AI
Dallas, Texas
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Job Description:
We are seeking a Staff Equipment Engineer to lead the development, sustainment, and improvement of production equipment, test racks, and test cells supporting manufacturing and system-level testing. This role is highly hands-on and works closely with Manufacturing, Test, Quality, and Design Engineering teams to ensure equipment reliability, scalability, and readiness for production. The ideal candidate has deep experience supporting complex electromechanical equipment in a production environment and driving improvements across safety, uptime, and throughput.
\n
What you'll do:
Own the technical lifecycle of production equipment, test racks, and test cells, from production readiness through sustainment and continuous improvement
Lead troubleshooting and root-cause analysis of equipment failures, downtime events, and test anomalies; implement corrective and preventive actions
Drive equipment reliability, availability, and maintainability (RAM) improvements to support production goals
Develop and maintain equipment documentation including schematics, BOMs, calibration plans, maintenance procedures, and operating instructions
Collaborate with Manufacturing, Test, and Quality teams to ensure equipment meets production, safety, and compliance requirements
Support equipment upgrades, obsolescence management, and capacity expansion as production scales
Define and execute equipment acceptance testing, validation, and handoff to production
Mentor junior engineers and technicians and provide technical leadership across equipment-related efforts
Manage external vendors and integrators as needed for equipment design, build, or modification
Required qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related field
8+ years of experience supporting production equipment, test racks, or test cells in a manufacturing or test environment
Strong hands-on experience with electromechanical systems, controls, instrumentation, and data acquisition
Proven ability to troubleshoot complex equipment issues across hardware, software, and controls domains
Experience developing and maintaining technical documentation for production equipment

About Us
Founded in 2015 to develop the world’s first industrially scalable laser metal additive manufacturing solution, VulcanForms is reshaping how the world manufactures critical products. We build and operate advanced digital infrastructure that enables innovation, accelerates growth, and supports sustainability across aerospace, defense, medical, and other essential industries. Through our vertically integrated capabilities, including scalable additive manufacturing and precision machining, we deliver true end-to-end production at scale by combining cutting-edge technology with a foundation of proven industrial craftsmanship. Our team brings deep expertise in manufacturing, materials science, software, automation, and operations, united by a shared commitment to quality, curiosity, and accountability. We foster an inclusive culture where people take ownership, solve meaningful problems, and continuously learn, because we believe diverse perspectives lead to better outcomes.
Job Purpose
As the Director, Product Development Engineering (CNC Machining) at VulcanForms, you will serve as the strategic technical executive responsible for leading, scaling, and unifying our medical device product development engineering organization for precision subtractive manufacturing. In this high-visibility role, you will architect the overarching engineering strategy for multi-axis CNC machining platforms (5-axis milling, Swiss turning, EDM), advanced CAM workflows, fixture design, and post-processing integration specifically tailored for high-consequence medical device applications. Products in this portfolio are manufactured through laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF), with CNC machining performed on 3D-printed, near-net-shape substrates to achieve final geometry, tolerances, and surface finish. You will own the phase-gated pathway from medical device design input through process validation and a formal handover to Operations for full-rate serial production—translating customer requirements into scalable engineering frameworks that set industry standards for dimensional accuracy, surface finish, system reliability, and yield across our commercial medical programs. You will manage and grow a multidisciplinary team of senior, principal, and product development engineers while acting as a key technical authority across hardware, software, tooling, quality, and operations. By establishing rigorous engineering governance, driving Design for Manufacturability (DFM) methodologies, building robust inspection strategies, optimizing manufacturing workflows, and expanding customer technical partnerships, you will ensure VulcanForms delivers production-ready, implantable, and surgical-grade components for our most strategic medical device customers.
Key Responsibilities
Executive Engineering Leadership & Strategy: Define and execute the long-term roadmap for medical device product development engineering for subtractive (CNC) manufacturing, from customer design input through production release; establish organizational KPIs, engineering governance, and resource loading models to support rapid company scaling.
Phase-Gated Development & Transfer to Operations: Govern the end-to-end framework for transitioning complex multi-axis CNC machining processes, fixture architectures, and digital CAM workflows through a phase-gated development process (feasibility, process development, verification and validation via IQ/OQ/PQ, and pilot production) into high-volume serial production; define gate entry/exit criteria and lead a formal handover to Operations covering released process documentation, control plans, trained operators, and demonstrated process capability (Cpk), with defined post-transfer sustaining support.
Team Building & Talent Development: Build, mentor, and retain a world-class team of product development engineers, CAM programmers, tooling specialists, and technical leads; cultivate a culture of technical excellence, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Strategic Customer & Executive Engagement: Serve as the primary technical authority for tier-one medical device OEM customers, executive leadership, and strategic partners; lead high-stakes technical reviews, program launches, and co-development initiatives.
Top-Down DFM & Cross-Functional Governance: Institutionalize advanced Design for Manufacturability and Inspectability (DFM/DFI) methodologies, applied early in the medical device design cycle and tailored to precision CNC machining (milling, turning, grinding, EDM) and ensure seamless cross-functional integration with upstream processes (e.g., LPBF blank feeds) and downstream operations (heat treatment, passivation, surface finishing, and automated CMM inspection).
Manufacturing Workflow Optimization & Yield: Optimize end-to-end manufacturing workflows (cycle time, setup reduction, toolpath and fixture strategy, work-cell flow, and in-process automation) using lean and value stream mapping; drive organization-wide corrective and preventive action (CAPA) frameworks for complex machining defects, tool wear anomalies, and geometric stack-up issues, leveraging advanced data analytics, statistical process control (SPC), and iterative testing to maximize yield.
Inspection Methods, Quality & Compliance: Define risk-based inspection strategies across CMM, optical/vision metrology, surface roughness measurement, in-process probing, and CT scanning; lead test method validation (TMV) and measurement system analysis (gauge R&R); establish and govern standardized operating procedures (SOPs), tooling/fixturing baselines, First Article Inspection (FAI) protocols, and engineering change management processes compliant with ISO 13485 and FDA QMSR (21 CFR 820) requirements.
Qualifications
10+ years of progressive engineering and technical leadership experience in advanced subtractive manufacturing, with a proven track record of building and managing high-performing engineering teams in multi-axis CNC machining (5-axis milling, Swiss turning, EDM) for implantable and surgical medical device product development.
Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Manufacturing, Aerospace, or Systems Engineering; Master’s degree is preferred.
Demonstrated executive presence with a track record of driving cross-functional alignment across R&D, Operations, Quality, and Commercial teams while serving as a trusted technical partner to C-suite leadership and external customers.
Deep mastery of precision subtractive manufacturing fundamentals, including advanced multi-axis CNC machining, fixture design, tool path optimization, metallurgy, complex GD&T (ASME Y14.5), inspection methods (CMM, optical/vision metrology, surface profilometry, in-process probing, and CT), measurement system analysis (gauge R&R), and statistical process control (SPC).
Proven experience leading phase-gated medical device product development, through design transfer, process validation (IQ/OQ/PQ), and formal handover to Operations for full-rate serial production, under ISO 13485 and 21 CFR 820.
Strong expertise in manufacturing workflow optimization (lean, value stream mapping, cycle-time and setup reduction) and integrated manufacturing workflows, including hybrid manufacturing (additive-to-subtractive workflows), passivation, electropolishing, cleanroom packaging, and non-destructive testing (NDT).
Practical, hands-on manufacturing skills, including medical device cleaning and cleaning validation, cleanroom packaging and sterile barrier systems, and QC inspection (receiving, in-process, and final inspection using CMM, optical comparators, and manual gauging), with the ability to work directly on the shop floor alongside technicians and operators.
Preferred Qualifications
Prior experience building or scaling product development or application engineering departments within high-growth medical device or advanced manufacturing technology companies.
Experience processing 3D-printed metal substrates (e.g., LPBF parts), including datum establishment on as-built geometry, support removal, stock allowance management, and machining of near-net-shape features.
Experience with enterprise-level CAD/CAM software, machining simulation tools, and digital manufacturing suites (e.g., Siemens NX CAM, Mastercam, Esprit, Vericut).
Hands-on familiarity with medical-grade materials (Titanium Ti-6Al-4V ELI, CoCr, Stainless Steel 316L/17-4PH, PEEK) and associated cutting tool physics/coolant delivery methodologies.
Certified Quality Engineer (CQE) or Six Sigma Black Belt credentials.
